candidates.rationale: The API returns two disjoint mutable subslices and requires mid <= self.len(). Mutable-reference returns are unsupported, and sequence views cannot express the returned references' disjoint identity and write-back relationship to self.

The result condition depends on whether self.len() >= N and, on success, returns disjoint mutable references to the first array chunk and tail. Current vstd views cannot capture their aliasing and write-back behavior.

On a nonempty slice this returns disjoint mutable references to the first element and tail. Mutable-reference results are unsupported, and their coordinated write-back into the original slice is not representable by sequence views alone.

The successful result consists of disjoint mutable references to the prefix and final N-element array. Existing public vstd vocabulary cannot model their reference identity, separation, and write-back to self.

On a nonempty slice this returns disjoint mutable references to the last element and preceding slice. Sequence equality would omit the essential alias separation and write-back semantics, while mutable-reference returns are unsupported.

This updates the outer mutable slice reference to its tail while returning a mutable reference to the removed first element with the original lifetime. Current vstd lacks an abstraction for this reference reassignment, alias separation, and shared write-back provenance.
